guide.title: How to use Sales CRM
guide.intro: A short tour of what each part of the CRM is for and how to use it. Every section has links that open the app in the right place.

basics.title: Find your way around
basics.lead: The sidebar has every section, with the saved views below them. Whatever you filter or open goes into the URL, so any view can be bookmarked or shared.

steps.1: Switch between Companies, Deals and Forecast with the tabs at the top.
steps.2: Press <kbd>⌘K</kbd> or <kbd>/</kbd> to search companies and people from anywhere.
steps.3: Use the saved views in the sidebar: a team, a region, deals closing this quarter or slipping deals.
steps.4: Change the language with EN or ES in the header. The page and its filters stay as they are.

basics.alt: The companies table with the search open, finding companies and contacts

companies.title: Prioritize your accounts
companies.lead: The companies table shows each account's pipeline, win probability and last interaction, worked out from its deals and activities.

steps.1: Sort by clicking a column header, or with Sort by.
steps.2: Narrow the list with the owner, stage and last activity filters. Reset clears them.
steps.3: Click a company to open its sheet: contacts, activities, pipeline health, deals and score cards.
steps.4: Select rows to reassign or delete them together, with undo, or export the view to CSV.

companies.alt: The companies table with Halcyon Air's sheet open

deals.title: Move deals through the pipeline
deals.lead: The board has a column per stage. Company metrics come from their deals, so moving a card updates the table and the forecast.

steps.1: Drag a card to another stage. On a phone, press and hold it first.
steps.2: From the keyboard, focus a card's handle, press <kbd>Space</kbd>, move it with the arrow keys and press <kbd>Space</kbd> again.
steps.3: Or open the card's ⋯ menu and choose a stage under Move to.
steps.4: Click a card to edit the deal: amount, close date, stage, probability and forecast category.

deals.alt: The deals board, with a column per stage

forecast.title: Check the quarter's forecast
forecast.lead: The forecast answers the question every sales manager asks: will we hit the number? It adds up what's won and what's expected for this quarter or the next.

steps.1: Read the totals: quota, closed won, Commit, Best case, weighted pipeline and what's left to reach the quota.
steps.2: Follow the chart: won so far, and where Commit and Best case lead by the end of the quarter. Show the numbers has the same data as a table.
steps.3: Compare reps under By rep. Clicking a name narrows the whole forecast to them.
steps.4: From a deal's ⋯ menu, change its forecast category or push it to the next quarter.

forecast.alt: The forecast: totals, the quarter's progress chart and the breakdown by rep

contacts.title: Know who you're selling to
contacts.lead: Contacts are the people at each account and their role in the purchase: who decides, who champions you, who could stand in the way.

steps.1: Search by name, title, email or company, and filter by buying role.
steps.2: Open a contact to see their details, the account's open deals and their colleagues.
steps.3: Each company's sheet lists its buying committee, decision makers first.
steps.4: Add someone with New Contact, or from a company's sheet with Add contact.

contacts.alt: The contacts list with Olivia Chen's sheet open

activities.title: Plan the next step
activities.lead: Activities are the calls, meetings, emails and tasks with each account. Every open deal should have a next step.

steps.1: Work through To do: overdue first, then today and upcoming. Check one off when it's done.
steps.2: A completed activity becomes the company's last interaction in the table.
steps.3: No next step lists the deals closing this quarter with nothing planned. Plan next step fixes that in one go.
steps.4: Log something that already happened with New Activity and Already done.

activities.alt: Activities to do, grouped into overdue, today and upcoming, next to the deals with no next step

sequences.title: Automate outreach
sequences.lead: A sequence is a series of emails, calls and tasks on set days. Contacts go through it until they reply. In this demo, emails aren't really sent.

steps.1: Open a sequence to see its steps, a preview and who's enrolled.
steps.2: Write steps with variables like first_name or company. The preview fills them in for a real contact.
steps.3: Enroll Contacts adds people. Their calls and tasks show up in Activities.
steps.4: When someone answers, use Mark as replied and the sequence stops for them.

sequences.alt: A sequence's steps, the email preview and the enrolled contacts

demo.title: About this demo
demo.lead: Everything runs in your browser, with fictional companies and people.

steps.1: Changes are saved in this browser. Dates move forward every day, so the demo never looks stale.
steps.2: Reset demo data in the sidebar brings everything back, with undo.
steps.3: It works on phones too: filters move into a bottom sheet and the board scrolls sideways.
steps.4: Built with Next.js, React, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS. The code, and how it's built, is on GitHub.

demo.alt: The deals board on a phone
